title: Offsite billing manifest generator for air-gapped nodes
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Private/VPC customers who operate in air-gapped or restricted networks cannot reliably stream metering data to our hosted billing pipelines. Current approaches (periodic CSV dumps or ad-hoc archives) are error-prone: missing sequence information, unsigned files, unclear deltas vs full snapshots, and non-deterministic ordering cause mismatches in usage accounting and manual reconciliation overhead.

Goal: Build a robust, auditable 'offsite billing manifest' pipeline for on-prem collectors that produces signed, chunked, and versioned export bundles that: 1) preserve deterministic ordering for idempotent ingestion, 2) include compact metering summaries for quick reconciliation, 3) support incremental (delta) and full snapshot modes, and 4) carry cryptographic proofs (manifest signatures) so the central billing system can verify provenance without direct network access to the origin node.

Scope: Engineer the collector-side manifest generator, a light CLI for operators to package and sign exports, server-side ingestion verifier, and a reconciliation dry-run in the console that validates manifests before final ledger apply. This ticket covers the on-prem export format, signing scheme selection, uploader metadata, and ingestion verification contract. Implementation of the final ledger write/charge mapping will be covered in a follow-up (ENG-13762).

Non-goals: Implementing the final billing UI or customer invoice generation (handled downstream), or replacing existing streaming telemetry for connected clusters. This is specifically for delayed/offsite export patterns and edge-case resumability for air-gapped customers.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Collector can produce a .rwi (Redwood-Weighted-Inventory) export bundle containing: a compact summary JSON, ordered chunk files (ndjson), and a signed manifest.json. 2) Manifests include: export_id, sequence_range, checksum per chunk, export_mode (delta|snapshot), timestamp, collector_version, and public_key_id. 3) Export bundles can be verified by the central ingestion verifier with no external network calls other than public key lookup. 4) Verified bundles import deterministically into the staging ledger with no duplicate units when replayed multiple times. 5) Test vectors (small, medium, large) included in repo and CI that exercise missing-chunk, out-of-order, and corrupted-chunk failure modes. 6) Operator CLI documented in Confluence with example commands for offline media transfer and automated checks. 7) Security review sign-off obtained for the signing scheme and key lifecycle doc.
design_notes:
Design decisions and trade-offs considered: 
- Format: ndjson per chunk to allow streaming verification and partial reads vs single monolithic archive. Chosen: chunked ndjson + index in manifest for random access.
- Signing: Use Ed25519 for compact, fast verification and deterministic signatures. We considered RSA (larger but familiar HSM workflows) but Ed25519 reduces footprint for edge devices. Public keys will be registered with the customer's control plane during install and mirrored to the billing verifier at ingest time.
- Delta vs snapshot: Default to delta exports (changes since last exported sequence) to reduce transfer size, with a snapshot option for recovery. Delta semantics require strict monotonic sequence numbers attached to every usage envelope.
- Deterministic ordering: Usage envelopes include a tuple (collector_id, monotonic_seq, local_timestamp). The ingestion verifier enforces ordering by sequence and rejects any chunk that would create gaps unless a special 'gap-tolerant' flag with operator justification is set.
- Idempotency: Each envelope is assigned a globally stable envelope_id derived from (collector_id, monotonic_seq, sha256(payload)). Ingestion checks dedupe via envelope_id.
- Compression: Chunks are optionally compressed with zstd; manifest records compression codec and uncompressed checksums for verification.
- Manifest rotation: Support partitioned exports when bundles exceed configured size (default 200MB uncompressed) and generate parent_manifest pointers for multi-part exports.

Open questions: 
- Key rotation UX for long-lived private installs (proposal: periodic upload of new public_key_id via ControlPlane API and support for multi-key verification during a migration window).
- Legal/audit retention defaults for exports (propose 90 days by default, customer-configurable).
implementation_plan:
Milestones: 
1) Prototype manifest schema and local generator (week 1-2): create minimal ndjson chunk writer, manifest JSON schema, and local Ed25519 signer integration.
2) Ingestion verifier service (week 2-3): implement manifest validation, chunk checksum verification, sequence gap detection, envelope dedupe. Add idempotent import logic to staging ledger.
3) Operator CLI and docs (week 3): package generator into a small Go binary, CLI flags for snapshot|delta, compression, signing key path. Draft Confluence runbook for transfer.
4) Testing and CI (week 4): unit tests, integration tests with offline replay harness, and CI test vectors for corrupted/out-of-order chunks.
5) Security review & key lifecycle docs (week 4-5).

updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting with SRE and Security. Agreed Ed25519 for signatures after discussing HSM constraints on some customer hardware.

2026-03-04: First-pass manifest schema v0.1 committed to collector-protos. Includes export_id, chunks[], signature, and meta. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/collector-protos/commit/abc123 (placeholder)

2026-03-06: Prototype generator writes chunked ndjson + manifest and validates locally. Found ordering edge-case when two collectors with same time drift produce colliding monotonic_seq ranges; decided to prepend collector_id to monotonic sequence namespace.

2026-03-08: Security review triage: requested addition of public_key_id and key-rotation notes in manifest. Also requested guidance on safe default retention. Assigned follow-up: write key rotation proposal in Confluence.

2026-03-10: Integration test harness capable of injecting missing-chunk and corrupted-chunk scenarios. Verified ingestion verifier rejects corrupted chunks and accepts repaired bundles when parent_manifest present.
notes_for_reviewers: Review focus: manifest schema completeness, gap-tolerance policy, and idempotency approach. Confirm that the chosen signature scheme maps to our enterprise key management guidance. Security wants explicit fallback handling for legacy customers with RSA-only HSMs. Please review the prototype PR and leave inline comments on edge-case behaviors (e.g., multiple rapid restarts of collector causing sequence overlap).
test_plan:
- Unit tests for manifest schema validation and signature verification.
- Integration test: simulate a multi-day export with delta mode, transfer via file copy, ingest into verifier, ensure ledger totals match reference totals.
- Fault injection: missing chunk, truncated chunk, out-of-order chunk, duplicate chunk.
- Performance: generate 5GB export and verify verify-time < 2 minutes on billing-ingest machine with default resources.
- CI: add deterministic test vectors and a mock verifier into the billing-ingest pipeline.
